purpose: Loncastuximab tesirine is used to treat a type of blood cancer called large B-cell lymphoma in adults who have already tried at least two other treatments. It targets cancer cells directly to help slow or stop the cancer from growing. Your doctor may recommend it when other treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: This medicine is made up of two parts: an antibody that acts like a guided missile, seeking out a specific protein called CD19 found on cancer cells, and a powerful cell-killing drug attached to it. Once the antibody finds and attaches to the cancer cell, it delivers the cell-killing drug directly inside the cancer cell. This helps destroy the cancer cells while trying to limit damage to healthy cells nearby.
common_side_effects: Swelling in the body (especially in the face, hands, feet, or legs), feeling very tired, low blood cell counts (which can raise your risk of infection or bleeding), nausea, and abnormal liver blood test results. You may also notice rash or changes in your skin.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious fluid buildup in the body, which may affect your lungs and heart — tell your doctor right away if you feel short of breath or have sudden weight gain. It can lower your blood counts, making it easier to get infections or bleed. It may also cause serious skin reactions and liver problems. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should not use this medicine, as it can harm the baby. You will need regular blood tests to monitor your health during treatment.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (directly into a vein) by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital, usually once every three weeks. The exact dose is calculated based on your body size. Your doctor will decide how many treatment cycles you need based on how your body responds.
